overview: Scoping review following JBI guidance and reported with PRISMA-ScR, charting how engagement with epilepsy self-management apps is defined, measured and sustained, which features and clinician support accompany sustained use, which outcomes are reported alongside engagement, and who does not engage.
population: Reports of adults with epilepsy offered or using a self-management app with a seizure diary or medication reminder, 2012 onward, any design including qualitative studies and grey literature.
exposure: Offer of or use of a self-management app; features; clinician support around the app.
procedures: The library searches four databases, two app-evaluation repositories and epilepsy charity websites. Two reviewers screen titles and abstracts and full texts; one charts and the other verifies 20 percent. The charting form records engagement definition and measure, follow-up length, engagement levels over time, app features, clinician involvement, outcomes reported alongside engagement, and who was offered, installed and excluded.

outcomes.name: Engagement definitions and measures
outcomes.measure: Charted definition, measure and follow-up length of engagement in each report
outcomes.why: The first thing the clinic needs to set any engagement target (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Engagement over time
outcomes.measure: Charted engagement levels at each reported time point

outcomes.name: Features and clinician support accompanying sustained use
outcomes.measure: Charted features and clinician involvement in reports with engagement beyond three months

outcomes.name: Outcomes reported alongside engagement
outcomes.measure: Charted adherence, seizure recording and quality-of-life results, labelled as associations
outcomes.why: Shows what has and has not been linked to engagement.

outcomes.name: Offer, install and exclusion
outcomes.measure: Charted counts of who was offered an app, who installed it and who was excluded

feasibility: Six hours a week across two reviewers from October 2026 to June 2027; library support confirmed.
biasMitigation: Charting form tested on the seven retrieved records
Outcomes charted as associations, never as effects of engagement
Grey literature from epilepsy charities included

biasFlags.label: Selective reporting of engaged users
biasFlags.note: Many reports describe only people who kept using the app.

biasFlags.label: Commercial app reports
biasFlags.note: Developers may report favourable engagement; the source type is charted.

flags: Charting items limited to the five parts of the PCC question
parsimony.simplestPath: One PCC question, one charting form, descriptive map.

theoreticalFramework: JBI scoping review method; engagement features charted without imposing a behaviour-change framework.
summary: Protocol revised to the PCC question: definitions and measures as the primary charted concept, with duration, features and support, outcomes and access.
